GS Retail Evolving into a Lifestyle Platform [Click eStock] On July 21, Heungkuk Securities maintained its "Buy" investment rating on GS Retail and raised its target price from 33,000 won to 37,000 won. Park Jongryeol, a researcher at Heungkuk Securities, stated, "The current share price does not fully reflect the pace of earnings recovery and platform competitiveness. Furthermore, GS Retail’s stable cash generation and dividend attractiveness remain at a high level," adding, "GS Retail is a leading stock capable of stable corporate value growth based on its lifestyle platform competitiveness." According to Park, GS Retail has secured differentiated competitiveness through a business portfolio that links convenience stores, supermarkets, home shopping, and digital channels. He predicted that, going forward, expanding customer touchpoints, operational efficiency, and platform competitiveness, rather than increasing the number of stores, will be the core factors determining the company’s corporate value. He cited GS Retail’s ability to connect a wide array of lifestyle-oriented businesses on a single platform as its greatest competitive edge. The nationwide convenience store network and supermarket logistics infrastructure lay the foundation for its quick commerce and O4O (Online for Offline) strategies. The accumulation of customer data via membership and mobile services is continuously increasing customer loyalty. In addition, the expansion of private brand (PB) products, AI-driven product operations, and logistics optimization are cited as factors expected to improve mid- to long-term profitability. Park identified the key variables for GS Retail’s future share price as same-store sales growth at convenience stores, improvement in supermarket profitability, expansion of PB and food sales, the performance of quick commerce and O4O strategies, company-wide cost efficiency, and shareholder return policies. © The Asia Business Daily. title: Preview: Karol G Set to Launch Her Biggest Tour Yet This Week with Two Nights at Soldier Field - The Early Registration
content: Chicago will become the center of Karol G’s world this weekend when the Colombian superstar launches her massive Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour with back-to-back performances at Soldier Field. The tour’s first concerts are scheduled for this week, Friday, July 24 and Saturday, July 25, giving Chicago fans the first look at what its promoters have described as Karol G’s most ambitious and immersive live production to date. Both shows begin at 7 p.m., with Venezuelan singer-songwriter Elena Rose joining Karol G as the special guest. Karol G will use Soldier Field to introduce the tour to the world. That adds another layer of anticipation to a pair of concerts that were already among the biggest Latin music events on Chicago’s summer calendar. The scale of the Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour makes the opening weekend even more significant. Announced following Karol G’s history-making performances as the first Latina artist to headline Coachella, the yearlong tour includes more than 39 stadium concerts across North America, Latin America and Europe. After leaving Chicago, Karol G will visit stadiums throughout the United States and Canada before traveling through Latin America during the winter. The tour will eventually conclude with a European stadium run in the summer of 2027, including performances in Barcelona, Madrid, Paris, London, Amsterdam and Milan. The extensive itinerary and stadium-only scope make Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour Karol G’s biggest tour to date, a remarkable next step after the success of her record-breaking Mañana Será Bonito World Tour. That previous trek sold more than 2.3 million tickets across 62 performances, grossed more than $300 million and ended with four sold-out concerts at Madrid’s Santiago Bernabéu Stadium. Her new production will be built around Tropicoqueta, Karol G’s 2025 album and her fourth consecutive release to reach No. 1 on Billboard’s Top Latin Albums chart. The project also recorded the largest U.S. streaming week ever for a Latin album by a woman, further demonstrating how quickly Karol G’s audience has expanded beyond the traditional boundaries of Latin music. Fans can expect the colorful world and varied Latin influences of Tropicoqueta to shape the new show, alongside selections from a catalog that includes global hits such as “Tusa,” “Provenza,” “Bichota” and “TQG.” Although the complete production and setlist will remain a mystery until Friday night, Karol G’s recent stadium tours and Coachella performances suggest that Chicago can expect a large-scale visual spectacle designed for the biggest venues in the world. The Soldier Field concerts arrive at another high point in Karol G’s career. In addition to her historic Coachella appearance, she has accumulated more than 117 billion career streams, earned more than 310 RIAA Platinum certifications in the United States and became the first woman to debut at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with a Spanish-language album when Mañana Será Bonito topped the chart. Now she will begin her next chapter along Chicago’s lakefront. Karol G and Elena Rose will perform at Soldier Field on Friday, July 24, and Saturday, July 25. Parking lots open at 3 p.m., stadium doors open at 5 p.m. and both concerts are scheduled to begin at 7 p.m. If you haven’t already, buy your tickets now. title: Will new college board decide President Dr. G’s future at tonight’s special meeting? - Keys Weekly Newspapers
content: The board for the College of the Florida Keys could decide the future of President Jonathan “Dr. G” Gueverra tonight at a special meeting in the Upper Keys. Notice of the meeting came out after 5 p.m. last Friday. On the agenda are two items: The president’s contract and the college’s Big Pine Key property. The meeting will be held at 6:30 p.m. at the Upper Keys Center in Key Largo. A college board, with six new members appointed by Gov. Ron DeSantis this year, has questioned Gueverra’s contract and specifically why a previous board renewed it a year early in July 2025. Some members, including chairwoman Alexandria Suarez, have also been critical of the president over the governor’s veto of funding to upgrade the college’s air conditioning infrastructure. There were some heated exchanges between Gueverra and board members Suarez and Michael Downer over the contract during the May 26 and June 30 meetings. Gueverra has been with the college since 2012. His current contract lasts through June 2028. The college will also discuss the ongoing efforts to safely remove Key deer from the college’s Big Pine Key property. Last week, CFK said it is continuing to work with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) and Florida Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) for the safe removal. USFWS wildlife professionals continue to monitor the deer, which remain healthy while the agencies refine plans to safely remove them from the site. Since January, the agencies have been in communication about Key deer on the property, with planning for the removal beginning in March. Based on recommendations from USFWS wildlife professionals and cooperating veterinarians, removal efforts were delayed until a resident fawn reached 4 months of age to ensure it could safely leave with the adult deer. Through continuous monitoring, wildlife experts and cooperating veterinarians have confirmed that the deer are in good health and have access to sufficient and appropriate food and water sources. “I’ve examined the deer intermittently throughout their confinement at the old prison site. On each occasion I noted that all the deer appeared to be in excellent health. There was ample food and fresh water available to them at all times,” said veterinarian Dr. Douglas Mader. “There is an older fawn present with four adults, and the fawn also is in excellent condition and eating well on its own.” The College of the Florida Keys is continuing its pursuit to expand workforce training and educational opportunities for residents of the Florida Keys at the site on Big Pine Key. The college is seeking to bring Commercial Driver’s License (CDL) training to the site. The college originally shared its ideas with the community in 2019 at a county commission meeting. In 2021, after leasing the property from the state, the college held two community meetings in Big Pine Key. Since then, the college has pursued funding opportunities to support expansion of programs and services in the Lower Keys. title: GS Retail Launches Field-Centered AX Project..."Expanding Customer Value with Startups" - 스포츠조선
content:
By
																						
												SeHyeong, Kim GS Retail recently held a meet-up event for the fourth cohort of its open innovation program, "The GS Challenge Future Retail (Future Retail)." The company is moving ahead with proof-of-concept (PoC) projects based on field-centered AX with the startups selected in the final round. According to GS Retail on the 20th, the Future Retail Season 4 meet-up took place on the 16th at GS Tower in Gangnam-gu, Seoul. This year's program was run in a way that had business units first define the challenges they needed to solve, then identify startups with the right technologies and execution capabilities. Building on the technology-focused collaboration experience accumulated through the first to third cohorts, this year's program strengthened the link between business-unit challenges and startup technologies. GS Retail set key innovation areas, including data and AI intelligence, autonomous operation optimization, and digital engagement innovation, and selected five AI startups with the technologies and execution capabilities needed for real-world application. GS Retail's business units and the startups will begin carrying out a range of proof-of-concept projects for about four months through mid-November. Key tasks include analyzing customer behavior and purchasing patterns at fresh-food-focused stores using Vision AI, search optimization (GEO) to respond to changes in AI search environments, and AI-based CRM automation. Lee Seong-hwa, head of GS Retail's New Growth Division, said, "Through the Future Retail Season 4 meet-up, we will further develop Future Retail into an open innovation platform that connects on-the-ground problem solving with business application." title: New BMW R12 G/S GS Trophy Competition Bike unveiled - Bike Rider Magazine
content: BMW Motorrad has revealed a special R12 G/S GS Trophy Competition Bike that will be used by riders competing in the 2026 BMW Motorrad International GS Trophy in Romania. Based on the recently launched R12 G/S, the competition-ready machine has been developed specifically for the off-road event, although customers will also be able to configure a near-identical version through BMW’s options catalogue. The only notable differences between the factory competition bikes and customer versions are the event-specific decals. Powering the R12 G/S GS Trophy Competition Bike is an air/oil-cooled 1,170cc boxer twin that produces 107.5bhp at 7,000rpm and 115Nm of torque at 6,500rpm. The motorcycle is equipped with the Comfort Package, which includes Hill Start Control, Gear Shift Assist Pro, heated grips and cruise control. To better suit the demands of the GS Trophy, BMW has also fitted the bike with the Enduro Package Pro. This adds off-road tyres, an 18-inch rear wheel, handlebar risers and additional riding modes. Other accessories include engine protection bars, cylinder head covers, a Rally cockpit fairing, an Akrapovič silencer and a five-litre tank bag. The competition bike is finished in ‘Lightwhite uni’ paint scheme with red graphics on the fuel tank, a bright red seat and an integrated navigation system. The 2026 BMW Motorrad International GS Trophy will take place in Romania from September 13 to 18, where competitors will tackle a variety of terrain including mountain roads, forests, river crossings and small villages. title: This 10-Year-Old Japanese Sedan's Interior Is Better Than Most New German Rivals - CarBuzz
content: The fourth-generation Lexus GS proves that great cabin design doesn't expire with age. Marking the end of the GS nameplate, this surprisingly spirited midsize luxury sedan pairs impeccable build quality with timeless styling, premium materials, and ergonomics that still outshine many newer German competitors. Buyers have noticed. The final GS has held its value remarkably well, so don't expect bargain-bin pricing just because it's a decade old. Its combination of reliability, refinement, and a genuinely upscale interior keeps demand high, and used prices reflect that. The Lexus GS always occupied a sweet spot in the fiercely contested midsize luxury sedan segment. It combines the balanced handling of a rear-wheel-drive sports sedan with the supple ride, refinement, and rock-solid reliability that have long defined the Lexus brand. That formula earned it a loyal following, but it couldn't escape the market's relentless shift toward SUVs. Lexus finally pulled the plug on the GS after the 2020 model year, leaving the similarly sized but front-wheel-drive ES as its midsize luxury sedan. It's an understandable decision, even if the ES lacks the GS' driver-focused character. By 2019, the GS accounted for just four percent of Lexus' US sales, with only 3,378 examples finding homes that year. The fourth-generation version was introduced for the 2013 model year after making an unlikely debut during 2011 Monterey Car Week. It's the version to buy today because it represents the peak evolution of the GS formula, blending handsome styling, sharp dynamics, and quality that still feels competitive nearly a decade later. Lexus gave the car a mid-cycle refresh for 2016, sharpening the styling, updating the technology, and introducing the fire-breathing GS F V8 flagship. The cabin changed very little, though, so pre-facelift models shouldn't be dismissed outright. Even so, if your budget allows, the refreshed car is the better pick thanks to its improved technology, particularly when it comes to safety, and broader range of powertrain options. Performance enthusiasts should head straight for the GS F. Its naturally aspirated 5.0-liter V8 produces 467 horsepower and 389 pound-feet of torque, and its legendary durability already makes it feel like a future classic. Buyers who don't need that level of performance will still find plenty to like elsewhere in the lineup. Following the 2016 refresh, the range opened with the GS 200t, which used a turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-four producing 241 hp and 258 lb-ft. Above it sat the GS 350 with a then-new 3.5-liter V6 delivering 311 hp and 280 lb-ft, while the GS 450h paired a 3.5-liter V6 with an electric motor for a combined 338 hp and 254 lb-ft of torque. But powertrains are easy to compare – what makes the GS genuinely hard to replace is what happens once you're inside. The same philosophy that shaped the GS's rear-wheel-drive chassis – prioritize what matters, ignore what doesn't – defined its interior, too. The GS doesn't rely on flashy design tricks (ambient lighting, anyone?) or acres of digital screens to impress, and that's exactly why it has aged so gracefully. Instead of chasing the latest trends, Lexus focused on the fundamentals. The dashboard is clean and uncluttered, with physical buttons and knobs for the functions you use most, along with analog gauges, premium leather, genuine wood or aluminum trim, and soft-touch materials on nearly every surface your hands naturally reach. While there's still a 12.3-inch infotainment screen, it doesn't dominate the dash, and you won't find glossy piano-black panels waiting to collect fingerprints. One of the cabin's biggest highlights, and today, a genuine flex, is the beautifully refined analog clock sitting proudly at the center of the dash. It evokes the classic luxury sedans of the past, yet it's far more sophisticated than its traditional appearance suggests. Lexus machined the clock from a single ingot of aluminum, making it look like a high-end watch. Meanwhile, LED backlighting ensures it's easy to read at night, while GPS synchronization automatically adjusts the time when traveling across time zones. It's just the type of feature that reflects the GS' attention to detail. The rest of the cabin follows the same approach, packing in luxury features without making them feel overwhelming. Even standard models came well-equipped with power-adjustable heated front seats, dual-zone climate control, and keyless entry and start, while higher trims added ventilated seats, heated rear seats, premium semi-aniline leather upholstery, a power rear sunshade, and higher-quality dash accents. Audiophiles should also seek out models equipped with the available 17-speaker Mark Levinson surround-sound system, which remains one of the best factory audio systems of its era. The pre-facelifted GS shares the same basic cabin design, so buyers on a tighter budget won't be missing out too much. However, it lacks a few of the later car's finer touches, including the GPS-synchronized analog clock, the 4.2-inch multifunction display in the gauge cluster, and the updated steering wheel design. It also missed out on the Lexus Safety System+ suite of electronic driver-assist features that debuted with the 2016 update. The suite bundles Adaptive Cruise Control, Pre-Collision System with Pedestrian Detection, Lane Keep Assist, Automatic High Beams, Sway Warning, Traffic Sign Recognition, and more. As with most Lexus vehicles, the fourth-generation GS delivers impressive reliability. RepairPal gives it an above-average four-out-of-five-star reliability rating, ranking it among the best cars in its class, while listing annual repair costs as well below the segment average. CarComplaints also records relatively few owner-reported issues, though the car's initial 2013 model year seems to have significantly more reported issues than any other year, most of them electronic gremlins. Despite its strong reliability ratings, not every GS will be trouble-free. Like any aging luxury car, maintenance history matters far more than the badge on the hood. Make sure routine servicing has been carried out, inspect the suspension for wear (especially on higher-mileage cars), and verify that all recalls have been completed, including those affecting earlier model years related to the Takata airbag scandal. Ironically, the interior is not without one key quality issue, at least on pre-facelift GS models. The dashboard material can be susceptible to heat and prolonged sun exposure, causing the upper dash to become sticky or even crack over time. It's worth checking the dashboard and door panels for tackiness or discoloration before buying, although many affected cars have already been repaired. Lexus largely addressed the issue with the facelifted model. A quick look through the CarBuzz Marketplace and other popular classifieds shows that fourth-generation GS prices start below $10,000, but those cars are typically pre-facelift models with close to 200,000 miles on the odometer. Set a more realistic mileage cap of around 70,000 miles, and you'll find plenty of well-kept examples priced from roughly $20,000. If your sights are set on the updated 2016-2020 model, however, expect to spend at least $25,000 for a clean example with reasonable mileage. Those asking prices highlight just how well the GS has held its value. The 2016 lineup started at $45,615 for the GS 200t, powered by the turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder, while the much more common GS 350 carried a starting MSRP of $50,000. Considering that most low-mileage, facelifted GS 350s still command around half of their original sticker price nearly a decade later, depreciation has been surprisingly gentle. That's an impressive showing in a segment where many luxury sedans lose value rapidly during their first few years. The GS F sits in an entirely different league. Thanks to its naturally aspirated 2UR-GSE 5.0-liter V8 and growing reputation as a future classic, prices remain remarkably strong. Expect to pay at least $50,000, with clean, well-maintained examples more commonly advertised around $60,000. That's not far removed from the 2016 model's $84,440 starting MSRP. Now compare that with similarly aged BMW M5 and Mercedes-AMG E63 models, both of which have depreciated far more heavily despite offering comparable performance. The fourth-generation Lexus GS is proof that great luxury cars don't have to chase trends to stay relevant. Its well-built, thoughtfully designed cabin still feels special nearly a decade later, while strong reliability, a sporty rear-wheel-drive chassis, and impressive value retention only strengthen its appeal. If you're shopping for a used midsize luxury sedan and are the type who likes to hold on to a car, few alternatives blend craftsmanship, comfort, and driving enjoyment quite as convincingly. Just note that good examples are priced accordingly. We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful. title: Karol G's Blueprint for Modern Pop Stardom - Young Hollywood
content: The Colombian superstar's global takeover isn't just about music. It's a masterclass in color, confidence, and community. Karol G's rise to the top proves the old rules of pop stardom are over. We're breaking down how her vibrant visual identity and fan-first ethos created a global movement. The old playbook for becoming a global pop icon has been officially shredded. For decades, the path was narrow: sing in English, sand down your edges, and fit a pre-approved mold. But a new generation of artists is proving that true superstardom is built on authenticity, not assimilation. And right now, no one is making a more vibrant and compelling case for that than Karol G. The Colombian powerhouse isn't just topping charts; she's building an entire world. Her success is a technicolor phenomenon that moves through sight and sound in equal measure, proving that a powerful message, a distinct look, and a real community can resonate in any language. It’s a blueprint for stardom that feels radically new, yet fundamentally human. Let’s talk about the hair. When Karol G transitioned into her brilliant blue era, and later her radiant pink phase for the Mañana Será Bonito chapter, it was more than a style refresh. It became a powerful piece of visual branding, an immediate signifier of who she is and what her music feels like. It was a beacon that fans, and the world, could instantly recognize. This use of color is a core part of her genius. It’s an unspoken language that telegraphs emotion, confidence, and transformation. At her stadium shows, seas of pink wigs and merchandise aren’t just fans showing support; they’re participants in a shared visual experience. It transforms a concert into a collective statement, creating an instantly iconic image that spreads organically across every social feed on the planet. This is how you build a universe, not just a fanbase. For years, the industry pushed the idea that massive international success required 'crossing over' into English-language music. Karol G politely ignored that memo. By continuing to create primarily in Spanish, she has centered her culture and experience, inviting the world to meet her where she is. Spoiler alert: the world showed up. In a hyper-connected streaming era, authenticity is the ultimate currency, and her commitment to her language is a huge part of that. It allows the emotion and swagger in her delivery to land with its full, undiluted power. Listeners who don’t speak Spanish don’t feel excluded; they feel the confidence, the vulnerability, and the joy. It bypasses literal translation and connects on the level of pure feeling, proving that a banger is a banger in any tongue. Her music itself defies easy categorization, pulling from reggaeton, pop, and Latin trap to create a sound that is uniquely her own. This genre-fluid approach ensures her art is never static, always reflecting a genuine place of inspiration rather than chasing a trend. It’s another way she asserts her vision, free from the constraints of outdated industry boxes. Beyond the visuals and the sonics, the core of Karol G’s empire is the community she has cultivated. It’s built on the powerful concept of the 'Bichota'—a term she has helped popularize to mean a confident, empowered, and unapologetic woman. It’s not just a cool word; it’s an ethos. She doesn’t just perform for her fans; she empowers them. This idea of collective confidence is woven through her entire creative output. She shares her own journey of growth and self-love, creating a space where vulnerability is a strength. Her connection feels less like an artist-to-fan dynamic and more like a massive, global friend group where everyone is cheering each other on. It’s this profound sense of belonging that turns casual listeners into die-hard devotees. That fan connection is the engine behind her record-breaking tours and chart dominance. People aren’t just buying a ticket to hear songs they like; they’re showing up for a reaffirming, communal experience. It’s a testament to the fact that in 2024, the most powerful marketing tool is a genuine, two-way relationship built on respect and shared values. Karol G is more than a pop star. She's a cultural force demonstrating a new path forward. title: Florida waterfront seafood restaurant not closing despite rumor - Treasure Coast News
content: It’s business as usual at all eight Kyle G restaurants on the Treasure Coast, despite a rumor to the contrary, owner Kyle Greene told TCPalm on July 16. Greene does not plan to close any restaurants for any reason, including — as rumor has it — because of the death of Bob Eustace, who owned the property where Kyle G’s Prime Seafood & Steaks is on A1A in Jensen Beach. Eustace, whose family still owns the property, died over a year ago, on May 16, 2025. The Eustace mansion on A1A is famous for its Christmas lights display, which Elsa Eustace canceled in 2025 because of her husband’s death. In February, Greene closed Stuart Fish Grill, which he opened in March 2025 in the Plantation Plaza strip mall near Stuart Bowl, at 1624 S.E. Federal Highway. It was a tough location where the season never really kicked in, Greene said. In the same location, Greene took over the part-Greek, part-Italian Nostalgia Greek Italian Kouzina in June 2023 after Tom Bournas originally opened it in 2019. These Kyle G restaurants remain open with no plans to close, he said. 2025:Opened in The Shoppes at the Heart of Tradition, 10200 S.W. Discovery Way, Port St. Lucie 2024:Opened at 10228 S.W.
